newsitem.title: UK: Uk's Gatwick express places train order.
newsitem.headline: Uk's Gatwick express places train order.

text.p: The Gatwick Express train operator, owned by National Express Group Plc, on Monday placed a 100 million pounds ($163 million) order for new trains with GEC-Althsom Metro-Cammell.

The first of eight luxury trains, each with eight coaches, is due to be delivered in December 1998, with an entire fleet in full service on the London Victoria to Gatwick airport route by May 1999. GEC won against 20 international train operators and the deal will help secure 1,800 long-term jobs at its plant in central England.

Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine said, "Rail privatisation has opened the way for new investment and better services. At last our railways are free to raise standards and put the customer first. Today's announcement from Gatwick Express is great news for British industry and British jobs."

Under the deal, GEC-Alsthom will design and build the trains as well as maintain them. The service element accounts for half the value of the contract, which is the largest order for new trains since privatisation of the train operating companies (Tocs).
The new trains should cut the present 30-minute jouney time to Gatwick to 25 minutes and are capable of cutting that to 20 minutes if the track is upgraded.

Gatwick Express managing director Mac Mackintosh said the trains would create a new era for rail passengers. "We aim to make the on-board service more like an airline experience than a traditional train journey," he said.
The announcement was immediately attacked by pressure group Save Our Railways, however.
The group said it welcomed any order for new trains, but said the announcement needed to be put into perspective -- the locomotives currently used on the Gatwick Express are more than 30 years old.

In a statement, Save Our Railways said that investment in new trains was lagging behind that achieved by British Rail before privatisation and described as "derisory" the privatised rail industry's investment plans.

National Express, the buses and rail giant, won the Gatwick Express rail franchise in April 1996 for a 15-year term. Passenger volumes grew by three percent in the first year of private ownership, with market share and operating profits also rising.
